answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake, slashed on proven spam, while reputation only grows through attestations from established, non-kin peers. At dawn, a fresh identity looks like any other, but an attacker who spawns a nebula of fake agents must fund a stake for each one and wait for real peers to vouch, so each fake costs money and time. The tundra of untrusted identities stays frozen until each identity has paid its stake and earned independent attestations, making mass fakery expensive while honest newcomers pay a refundable deposit.
